findings_fixed: L30: DeveloperAreaGate now bypasses the administrator gate in production only under the proxy's exact double-flag pairing (PLAYWRIGHT_OFFLINE_MODE=true AND NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCKUPS_ENABLED=true), never the mockups flag alone; added a production-readiness assertion (mockupsGateProductionRisk) that fails when the flag is set alone in a production-like environment.

L31: added DeveloperAreaRouteGuard, a client component wrapping the gate's authorized children that calls router.refresh() on every pathname change within a gated subtree, forcing the server tree (including DeveloperAreaGate) to re-run on soft client-side navigation between sibling hub pages instead of reusing a cached already-authorized payload.
L32: added the ingestion_admin consumeApiRateLimit guard to /api/ingestion/jobs, matching its sibling /api/ingestion/quality.
L43: added the same rate-limit guard to the remaining unlimited administrator ingestion routes: /api/ingestion/batches, /api/ingestion/jobs/[id]/retry (the mutating retry POST), and /api/jobs.

L29: /api/health now reclassifies an unauthorized deep probe (checks.supabase = "unauthorized") as HTTP 401 instead of folding it into the same 503 "degraded" shape as a genuine outage; a real Supabase outage on an authorized probe is unchanged (still 503). /api/health/ready now caches its whole computed result in-process for 2 seconds so a burst of hits shares one Supabase probe instead of one each, without needing a durable rate limiter that would itself require a database round trip.

M11: /api/ingestion/quality now bounds document_pages, document_images, ingestion_jobs and ingestion_job_stages reads with an explicit 1,000-row cap (CHILD_QUERY_ROW_CAP), and reports partial: true plus partialTables in the response when any of those reads land exactly on the cap, instead of staying silent about possible truncation.

L14: FreshnessStamp (Server Component) and IngestionPanel's client-side CheckedAt now both pin timeZone: Australia/Perth and print the zone name, closing the unlabelled eight-hour gap between the container clock (UTC) and the browser clock on the one page that polls live.

L15: /api/ingestion/jobs now runs a third query (failedCountQuery, mirroring activeCountQuery's shape) and returns failedJobCount as a pre-pagination full count; the ingestion panel's 'failed jobs' tile now renders that instead of the page-scoped failed.length, matching how the 'active jobs' tile already works.

L80: corrected the JSDoc comment above the hub's EnvironmentStrip that claimed the document count is scoped by row-level security; it is scoped by an explicit owner_id filter on a service-role admin client, which bypasses RLS entirely.

L82: reworded the routes panel's blanket 'These do not exist in production' claim, which was false for the four developer-gated subtrees (the page itself is one of them), to name the exception and the administrator-sign-in requirement.

L76: updated the Development hub's Care Plan card summary from the stale August 'Stage B prototype' text to name all five areas the prototype now covers (Management Plan, ED Presentations, Personal Safety Plan, Patient Plan, Reviews/Team/Governance), verified against operations-pages.tsx's ReviewsSurface/TeamSurface/GovernanceSurface.

L69: added two new Playwright/vitest cases to tests/proxy.test.ts (no existing case changed) covering the previously-untested ward-flow prefix for shouldBlockProductionMockups and iterating DEVELOPER_GATED_PATH_PREFIXES for the x-developer-area header test, so a regression dropping a prefix can no longer hide behind partial coverage.

L121: added one disclosure sentence to the Review state page's scope paragraph explaining that review records refresh only when the snapshot is regenerated (npm run docs:update) and that the page's own freshness stamp does not move for a review-record append, since review_state is deliberately excluded from the staleness comparison.

L81: reworded the routes card's 'Every page and all 15 modes' (stale; app-modes.ts has carried 16 modes) to the count-free 'Every page and every app mode', matching the routes page's own snapshot-derived 'App modes · 16' heading.

L30 (a/b/d): developerGateBypassAllowed() is strictly narrower than the old mockupsEnabled() — identical outside production (both always true), and in production it now needs PLAYWRIGHT_OFFLINE_MODE=true AND NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCKUPS_ENABLED=true, the exact pairing src/proxy.ts:280 uses and the one scripts/run-playwright.mjs:376-377 sets for the @mockup project. The Playwright offline exception from the Stage-5 note is honoured. The readiness assertion fails only on flag-alone-in-production and warns on the pairing; both branches are unit-tested. Tests fail without the fix (the predicate did not exist).

L31 residual (not blocking, package note explicitly allows a client hook): the guard fires router.refresh() after the soft navigation completes, so the sibling page's RSC payload for e.g. /mockups/development/ledger is still served once by the server (which does not re-run the layout gate on partial render) before the refresh re-runs DeveloperAreaGate and swaps in the sign-in screen. That is a one-render window on repository-metadata pages only; a per-page resolveDeveloperAccessState() call would close it fully. Worth stating in the PR body.

L32/L43 budget: all four admin routes now share the one `ingestion_admin` bucket at 60 requests/min (src/lib/api-rate-limit.ts:90). ClinicalDashboard polls jobs+batches+quality together every 5 s during active indexing (36/min) and the hub panel adds 12/min — 48/min for one administrator with both open, so a second dashboard tab during a long ingestion would trip 429s. The hub panel treats 429 as a transient fetch error (ingestion-panel.tsx:245-253), so it degrades correctly; the dashboard is outside this package. Consider raising ingestion_admin to 120/min or giving the polled GETs their own bucket in a follow-up.

M11: the explicit 1,000-row cap plus `partial`/`partialTables` is real and tested (a 1,000-row page mock returns partial: true; a 1-row mock returns neither field). Two halves of the finding are not closed and were not disclosed: (1) the only consumer, src/components/ClinicalDashboard.tsx:1001, does not read `partial`, so the console still shows a capped result as if complete — the package note asked to 'surface more than N'; ClinicalDashboard.tsx is outside p5's owned files, so this belongs in the PR body as residual; (2) `text` is still selected in full only to be measured with `.trim().length < 80`, so the bandwidth half of the finding remains. Also, exactly 1,000 real rows will read as partial (false positive, conservative direction).

L29: the reclassification is done in the route, not in healthResponse(), so /api/health/ready (allowUnauthenticatedDeep: true) cannot hit it — verified in src/lib/health-response.ts:36-38. Minor: the 401 body still carries `status: "degraded"` from healthResponse(); only the HTTP status changed. No test, doc or script pins the old 503 shape (grep for deep=1 across tests/*.spec.ts, docs, scripts: only authorized-probe usages). The 2 s readiness cache is module-level and also caches a 503 for 2 s after recovery — harmless.

L14: the server stamp appends a literal ' AWST' because Intl rejects timeZoneName with dateStyle/timeStyle (true); the client stamp uses timeZoneName: 'short' which yields 'AWST' under ICU. Both tests assert /AWST/. Perth has no DST, so the literal is correct year-round.
